jobs.title: Researcher, Cyber Safety Training
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM Safety Research at OpenAI is responsible for ensuring our most capable models can be safely deployed in the real world. The Safety Training team develops the research and engineering methods that shape model behavior through post-training, reinforcement learning, evaluation, and deployment feedback. Our work focuses on making models helpful, reliable, and aligned with safety policies across model types, modalities, and product surfaces. We work across both longer-term safety research and the core post-training work needed to improve production models. ABOUT THE ROLE You’ll work directly on the large training runs that shape OpenAI’s frontier models. Your focus will be teaching models to help people do legitimate security work while recognizing when their assistance could enable harm. A model that refuses to help a defender investigate a security issue can fail in a different way from one that helps someone misuse it. You’ll study both kinds of mistakes and use what you learn to improve the next training run. We’re looking for someone with hands-on machine learning experience who wants to bring security judgment into model training. You might come from cybersecurity and want to go deeper on post-training, or from reinforcement learning and want to build substantial expertise in cybersecurity. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL - Work with cybersecurity researchers to identify situations where context changes what help a model should give. - Design complex and realistic cyber safety evaluations. - Research post-training techniques that robustly improves the cyber safety of the frontier models. - Work with the core post-training team to bring promising methods into large model runs and verify that the safety improvements hold at scale. - Coordinate and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including T&S, legal, policy and other research teams, to ensure that our products meet the highest safety standards. jobs.title: Research Operations, External Artifacts
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Every time Anthropic releases a model, we publish a system card: a long-form technical document that describes the model's capabilities, safety properties, evaluation results, and the reasoning behind our deployment decisions. System cards are some of the most consequential and widely read documents we produce, and they are one way we hold ourselves publicly accountable for the safety claims we make. We're hiring a Research Operations Specialist to help own system card production. You'll work embedded with research and safety teams through each launch, coordinating contributions from dozens of researchers, holding the schedule and the open-threads list, and making sure the document ships on time as a single, accurate, internally consistent whole. Along the way you'll do real editorial work: turning results and researcher notes into clear, honest prose and pushing back when an explanation doesn't hold together. System cards sit within a wider family of external safety artifacts, including risk reports and Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) updates. Part of this role is keeping the system card consistent with those documents so that Anthropic's public safety story reads as one coherent account rather than several. This role sits in Research Operations and works closely with Alignment, Safeguards, Frontier Red Team, and capabilities research. The core of the job is part project management, part translation: keeping a complex, many-author, hard-deadline document on track while making frontier safety research legible to researchers, policymakers, journalists, and the public — without sacrificing precision. jobs.title: Astrodynamics Lead (Founding Role)
jobs.description: About Apolink Apolink is building the first-ever backward-compatible data relay constellation in low Earth orbit. By enabling efficient data aggregation and relay through our hybrid RF-optical inter-satellite link (ISL) architecture, we support scalable and resilient space infrastructure across commercial, federal, and defense applications. About The Role In this role, you'll design the constellation, verify RAAN and phasing, and run the coverage analysis that shows which architectures meet customer SLAs. You'll also build the propulsion and Δv budgets for deployment, station-keeping, collision avoidance, and de-orbit. This starts with our upcoming paired demonstration satellite mission and scales to the full LEO relay constellation. You'll work directly with the bus, propulsion, and optical/RF link teams and turn orbital analysis into hardware and mission requirements. The role is hands-on end to end: modeling, trade studies, maneuver planning, and on-orbit operations. Responsibilities: - Design and own constellation architecture: plane count, altitude, inclination, LTAN, and intra- and inter-plane phasing, traded against coverage, launch cost, and ISL geometry - Run SLA-grade coverage analysis on link-closing access: handover continuity, window durations, gap statistics, and percent-time-covered for specific target orbits. - Work with the RF team to close coverage and access analysis against real RF link budgets rather than geometric visibility alone. This means computing access windows only where range, elevation, off-boresight angle, Doppler, and slant-path losses support the required data rate and margin. - Model ISL relative geometry between constellation members and customer spacecraft, including range, angular constraints, and handover timing. Iterate with the RF and optical teams so orbit design and link design converge. - Develop Δv and propellant budgets for drag makeup across the solar cycle, station-keeping, collision avoidance, and end-of-life disposal
